attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known source theorem proves C_{H_k}(N)>N^{1+epsilon} for unbounded k with a common epsilon against general nonuniform circuits.
steps: Assume for contradiction that SAT has circuits of size O(n^c) for some fixed c.
Choose k from the source hypothesis with c/k<1+epsilon.
Construct a circuit for H_k on length N=n^k by checking the padding pattern in O(N) gates and running the SAT circuit on the first n=N^{1/k} bits.
Since max{1,c/k}<1+epsilon, the upper bound is eventually below N^{1+epsilon}.
Contradict the asserted source lower bound for H_k at that k.
Because c was arbitrary only under the forall c exists k source quantifier, derive SAT notin P/poly conditionally.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid conditional bridge, not a proof of P != NP. The hard work is the unproved source lower-bound family, which must also evade natural-proofs and relativization-style obstructions.

assumptions: Circuit model is nonuniform fan-in two Boolean circuits over total length-N functions.
The lower bound is eventual over padded lengths N=n^k; an i.o. version gives only the corresponding i.o. contradiction.
The exponent epsilon is independent of N and must remain positive after the padding overhead.
The source claim is not a compressed-input SAT lower bound in disguise.
definitions: source object: H_k=Pad_k(SAT), the total padded SAT language at lengths N=n^k, measured by nonuniform Boolean circuit size C_{H_k}(N).
target object: SAT circuit lower bounds C_{SAT}(n) notin O(n^c) for every fixed c, implying NP not subset P/poly.
controlled interface: the uniform padding map R_k(x)=x10^{n^k-n-1} and circuit pullback/pushforward with an explicit O(N)-size padding-validity checker.

target-preserving condition: for each target exponent c one must have a source lower bound for some k satisfying c/k<1+epsilon on all sufficiently large padded lengths, with no advice depending on x beyond length.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: any proof using one fixed k, a finite set of k values, or a threshold swallowed by the O(N) checker cannot validly imply NP not subset P/poly.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Repaired route-level bridge: it gives an exact quantitative transfer and isolates the additional quantifier needed for a P/poly consequence.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Fix epsilon>0. Let H_k=Pad_k(SAT). If for every target exponent c there is a padding parameter k with c/k<1+epsilon such that C_{H_k}(N)>N^{1+epsilon} on all sufficiently large padded lengths N=n^k, then SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for every c, hence NP is not contained in P/poly. For one fixed k the same bridge excludes only c<k(1+epsilon).

assumptions: No independent amplification changes k or epsilon.
The only reduction used is padding plus total-language checking.
definitions: source object: one fixed padded carrier H_k with threshold N^{1+epsilon}.
target object: finite-exponent SAT lower bounds below n^{k(1+epsilon)}.
controlled interface: same padding simulation as L2.uniform_padding_exponent_bridge.
target-preserving condition: the target exponent must lie strictly below k(1+epsilon).

equations.label: excluded_exponent_window
equations.valid_when: Applies in the fixed-k regime where no second theorem amplifies the padding parameter.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: k=2 and epsilon=0.01 cannot refute SAT in SIZE(n^3), since c/k=1.5 exceeds 1.01.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantine lemma preventing route overclaim from a finite-exponent separation to P/poly separation.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For fixed k and epsilon, a lower bound C_{H_k}(N)>N^{1+epsilon} cannot by padding alone exclude SAT circuits of size n^c when c>=k(1+epsilon). The simulated H_k circuit then has size O(N^{c/k}), which is not below the source threshold.

assumptions: Standard PRF-based natural-proofs barrier is treated as a conditional obstruction, not a theorem ruling out every method.
Relativization blocks the bridge only if the source theorem relativizes and purports to separate relativizing worlds.
definitions: source object: lower-bound method proving C_{H_k}(N)>N^{1+epsilon}.
target object: nonuniform circuit separation for SAT.
controlled interface: the bridge transfers only size exponents, not barrier-escaping structure.
target-preserving condition: the source lower-bound proof must avoid becoming a large constructive useful property for general circuit lower bounds.

equations.latex: \text{padding transfer is valid}\;\not\Rightarrow\;\text{source lower bound avoids naturalness}
equations.valid_when: Valid when auditing the route separates the conditional bridge from the unproved lower-bound machinery.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: falsifier: a claimed generic constructive density-heavy property proving H_k hardness would be natural and therefore not a valid barrier-escaping source theorem.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier interaction ledger: it locates the obstruction in proving the source lower bounds, not in the exponent transfer.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The padding bridge itself is relativizing and algebraically inert; it is not the nonrelativizing ingredient. Any source lower-bound proof for H_k that works by a large constructive property against general circuits risks the natural-proofs obstruction under PRF assumptions, so the source proof must be non-natural, explicit-singleton, or outside that scope.

Need total nonuniform circuit lower bounds C_{H_k}(N)>N^{1+epsilon} for arbitrarily large k, not promise-only or compressed-input claims.
One k gives SAT notin SIZE(n^c) only for c<k(1+epsilon); P/poly exclusion requires forall c exists k with strict margin.
Padding transfer is relativizing; barrier avoidance must occur in the source lower-bound proof, especially against natural-proofs-style largeness and constructivity.

falsifier: if lower bounds hold for only finitely many k, every c above (1+epsilon) max k remains unaddressed.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The argument only blocks fully relativizing, target-preserving templates. It does not evaluate a route whose decisive step is nonrelativizing, non-natural, or non-algebrizing in a formally specified way.
steps: Type the source model as deterministic oracle Turing machines plus the canonical bounded NP^O-complete language K^O.
Assume a sound proof template T has a uniform oracle lift L(T,O) preserving every inference and polynomial-time reduction.
Under target preservation, a T-proof of K^emptyset notin union_c DTIME(n^c) becomes, for every oracle O, a proof of K^O notin union_c DTIME^O(n^c).
Instantiate O by a Baker-Gill-Solovay collapsing oracle A with P^A=NP^A.
Because K^A is NP^A-complete and P^A=NP^A, K^A lies in P^A, hence in DTIME^A(n^d) for some fixed d.
This contradicts the transferred lower bound, so no sound route satisfying RelTP(T) can establish the target.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a negative audit of a proof interface. It separates bad routes from admissible ones but proves no lower bound for K in the real, unrelativized world.

assumptions: K^O is complete for NP^O under polynomial-time many-one reductions with oracle access to O.
T is a sound finite or recursively enumerable proof template whose semantic inferences remain sound after replacing all machines by oracle machines.
The oracle lift preserves the quantitative threshold union_c DTIME(n^c), allowing only fixed polynomial reindexing of exponents.
There exists a Baker-Gill-Solovay oracle A such that P^A=NP^A.
The conclusion is a route-level quarantine, not a proof of P != NP.
definitions: source object: a uniformly relativizing proof template T for deterministic oracle Turing-machine lower bounds on the canonical bounded oracle-NP complete language K^O, claiming K^emptyset notin DTIME(n^c) for all fixed c.
target object: P != NP via K^emptyset notin P, with the oracle target family K^O notin P^O used only for the barrier audit.
controlled interface: proposed lower-bound method -> relativization audit, formalized by an oracle-lift map L(T,O) preserving each inference, reduction, and machine simulation.
target-preserving condition: if T proves the unrelativized polynomial-time lower bound, then L(T,O) proves the same fixed-exponent lower bound against DTIME^O(n^c) for every oracle O.

equations.label: target_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when K is the fixed NP-complete language and the intended target is a uniform polynomial-time lower bound.

equations.label: relativizing_transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies when every proof inference has a uniform oracle lift and preserves all fixed polynomial exponents.

equations.label: bgs_falsifier
equations.valid_when: Valid when K^A is chosen complete for NP^A under oracle polynomial-time reductions.

equations.label: quarantine_conclusion
equations.valid_when: Requires the target-preserving complexity-class transfer and the BGS collapsing oracle in the same oracle convention.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is an explicitly nonrelativizing inference, such as arithmetization or interactive-checking algebra, whose correctness is not preserved by arbitrary oracle substitution.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Certifies failure of fully black-box relativizing lower-bound routes at the exact P-polynomial threshold.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A sound lower-bound template for the canonical NP-complete language K cannot both relativize uniformly and preserve the P-vs-NP target threshold. If it did, a proof of K notin P would transfer to K^O notin P^O for every oracle O, contradicting a BGS oracle A with P^A=NP^A.

assumptions: R has density delta_N under the uniform distribution on n-bit Boolean functions.
R is useful against SIZE(n^k): no n^k-size truth-table function satisfies R.
The PRF family maps seeds to truth tables of functions computable by circuits of size n^k.
The distinguisher receives full truth-table access, so its running time is measured in N=2^n.
definitions: source object: a Razborov-Rudich style property R_N subseteq {0,1}^{2^n} decidable in time N^b, where N=2^n.
target object: circuit lower bound K notin SIZE(n^k), used only as a proof-object audit against pseudorandom function barriers.
controlled interface: lower-bound property -> natural-proof audit, exposing constructivity, largeness, usefulness, and truth-table access.
target-preserving condition: usefulness must reject every function computed by circuits of size n^k, including each output function generated by the candidate PRF family.

equations.label: density
equations.valid_when: Valid when the property is evaluated over complete truth tables of n-variable Boolean functions.

equations.label: prf_rejection
equations.valid_when: Valid when every PRF output function lies inside the circuit class against which R is useful.

equations.label: advantage
equations.valid_when: Applies after constructivity gives the distinguisher enough time to evaluate R on the full truth table.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma is falsified for this route if R is non-large, nonconstructive, not useful against the PRF circuit size, or does not operate on full truth tables.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quantifies the natural-proof obstruction so future routes must name a real escape feature instead of only saying nonstandard.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A poly(N)-constructive property R of n-bit truth tables with density delta_N that is useful against SIZE(n^k) yields a full-truth-table distinguisher of advantage at least delta_N against any PRF family whose n-bit output functions have size at most n^k. Thus the natural-proof route must escape by non-largeness, nonconstructivity, non-black-box access, or by targeting a regime below the PRF threshold.

The prior N^{-a}-density truth-table distinguisher calculation remains active; any natural property route must specify its escape feature before promotion.
If a route claims arithmetization as the escape from relativization, the next valid test is whether the proof still algebrizes under low-degree oracle extensions.

falsifier: show the route uses algebraic extension queries in a way that is nonrelativizing and then pass a separate algebrization audit.
falsifier: demonstrate that the claimed lower bound is for a nonuniform or promise target that no longer transfers to K notin P.
falsifier: quantify a threshold loss where K notin DTIME(n^c) transfers only to a subpolynomial or advice-bearing statement, not to P != NP.

This is meaningful route-level progress: it certifies a class of proof objects as invalid while leaving P != NP untouched.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No known SAT-to-MCSP reduction supplies a no-side gap s>=N^epsilon with uniform length balance. Ordinary MCSP-hardness conjectures, Turing reductions, or reductions with tiny thresholds do not provide this carrier.
steps: Start with the stronger-than-folklore source model: a length-balanced gap Karp reduction R from SAT to LowMCSP with no-instances mapped to CC>N^epsilon.
Choose a canonical unsatisfiable 3CNF family psi_m, e.g. z AND not z padded to length m, so the SAT answer is known without solving SAT.
Compute R(psi_m)=(x_m,s_m). By correctness, x_m is high-complexity on the no side; no MCSP decision procedure is invoked.
Use length balance m<=N_m^k to output x_m in poly(N_m) time, hence in E after interpreting x_m as a truth table.
Pad to the next power of two and lose only O(log N_m) gates when restricting a small circuit for the padded function back to x_m.
Conclude an i.o. E lower bound CC(L_n)>2^{epsilon' n} on the image lengths for every epsilon'<epsilon.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation is a conditional bridge lemma. It neither proves the source reduction nor implies P != NP; it only shows that such a reduction would already contain explicit lower-bound content.

assumptions: R is uniform and runs in m^{O(1)} time.
There is a fixed epsilon>0 with no-side gap s_phi>=N_phi^epsilon.
For infinitely many canonical contradictions psi_m, N_{psi_m} tends to infinity and m<=N_{psi_m}^k.
Circuit size is measured for Boolean circuits computing the truth table function; padding overhead is O(log N).
definitions: source object: a deterministic polynomial-time reduction R that maps a 3CNF phi of length m to (x_phi,s_phi), where x_phi has length N_phi, and phi unsat implies CC(x_phi)>s_phi>=N_phi^epsilon.
target object: an E-uniform language L whose length-n truth table equals a padded x_{psi_m} on infinitely many n, with CC(L_n)>2^{epsilon' n}.
controlled interface: feed only canonical unsatisfiable formulas psi_m into R; use no MCSP oracle, no advice string, and no search over truth tables.
target-preserving condition: the output lengths are unbounded and length-balanced, m<=N_phi^k, and padding from N_phi to a power of two loses only o(N_phi^{epsilon'}).

equations.label: threshold-transfer
equations.valid_when: Valid when n_m=ceil(log N_m), epsilon'<epsilon, and padding changes length by less than a factor two.

equations.label: uniform-output-time
equations.valid_when: Valid when the reduction is length-balanced on the canonical contradiction family and no nonuniform advice is used.

equations.label: lower-bound-instance
equations.valid_when: Applies after the padded truth table still restricts to the original high-MCSP string with only comparator overhead.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is any reduction whose no-side threshold is o(N^epsilon), whose output length is not balanced, or whose construction uses advice.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Bridge lemma: it converts a named MCSP gap-reduction source into an explicit E lower-bound target with quantitative threshold preservation.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If a uniform length-balanced many-one gap reduction from SAT to LowMCSP maps every no-instance to a truth table of circuit complexity at least N^epsilon, then canonical contradictions yield an explicit high-MCSP carrier and an i.o. E circuit lower bound of size 2^{epsilon' n} for every epsilon'<epsilon. This is route-level progress, not P != NP.

assumptions: A is uniform and deterministic.
A(1^n) runs in 2^{O(n)} time and outputs exactly 2^n bits.
CC(A(1^n))>2^{epsilon n} for all sufficiently large n.
definitions: HighMCSP_epsilon(N) means strings x in {0,1}^N with Boolean circuit complexity greater than N^epsilon.
The target language L_A has L_A(u) equal to the u-indexed bit of A(1^{|u|}).
The IW consequence requires hardness on all sufficiently large input lengths, not merely infinitely often.

equations.label: mcsp-to-size
equations.valid_when: Valid when N=2^n and the MCSP threshold is measured on the full length-n truth table.

equations.label: iw-use
equations.valid_when: Requires the hardness bound for all sufficiently large lengths and the standard Impagliazzo-Wigderson uniform computability hypothesis.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the carrier is only infinitely often, IW gives at most an i.o. derandomization variant, not full BPP=P.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Extraction theorem already available once the source carrier is uniform; the unresolved task is source construction.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A deterministic poly(N)-time generator outputting, for every n, a length N=2^n truth table with CC>N^epsilon gives a language in E with 2^{epsilon n} circuit lower bounds and supplies the standard IW hardness hypothesis for BPP=P.

assumptions: The advice may encode the hard truth table or the choice of a hard candidate.
No canonical, efficiently computable selector for a_n is provided.
definitions: Advice leakage means x_n is produced by A(1^n,a_n) with |a_n|>O(1) and no uniform way to recover a_n in 2^{O(n)} time.
The target-preserving transfer requires a single E machine deciding all bits of L.
The obstruction is nonrelativizing only if the advice is eliminated by an arithmetized or diagonal uniform construction; otherwise it is merely outside the target model.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier can be extracted from the no side of a length-balanced gap reduction using canonical contradictions; high complexity must be explicit in the reduction's soundness clause.
Uniform high truth tables at threshold N^epsilon transfer to i.o. E lower bounds; all-length carriers give the IW derandomization hypothesis.
Explicitness is poly(N) output time with no advice; length balance m<=N^k is now a formal obligation for reduction-based carriers.

falsifiers: falsifier: the reduction outputs N_m much smaller than m^{c}, so computing the carrier costs super-polynomial time in its truth-table length.
falsifier: the no-side MCSP threshold is logarithmic, polylogarithmic, or otherwise below N^epsilon, causing quantitative threshold collapse.
falsifier: the construction needs advice to choose the hard MCSP instance, so the target becomes nonuniform and the IW transfer is not valid.
falsifier: the reduction is a Turing reduction whose accepting path depends on unknown SAT answers, so a fixed contradiction does not expose a single high truth table.
falsifier: the output is an MCSP yes-instance on contradictions under the chosen convention; then it certifies low complexity rather than high complexity.
